observation: The report states all 219 test executions have timestamps/durations/evidence, but the reconciled inventory is 209 PASS, 2 BLOCKED, 8 NOT RUN.
impact: A blocked or not-run case was not successfully executed as a passing test. This wording can overstate executed coverage.
required_action: Use separate fields: disposition/reconciled_at for every case; executed_at/duration only when actually executed. Change narrative to 219 cases reconciled, 209 passed, 2 blocked, 8 not run.

observation: The report labels overall pass rate 99.1% while its stated formula is PASS/(PASS+FAIL). With 209 PASS and 0 FAIL, that formula gives 100% for executed, decisive test outcomes; 209/219 planned cases is 95.4%. 209/(209+2) is approximately 99.1%, but includes BLOCKED and excludes NOT RUN.
impact: Readers may interpret the wrong denominator as a reliability figure.
required_action: Define at least two metrics: executed-test pass rate = PASS/(PASS+FAIL) if blocked/not-run are excluded; inventory completion/pass coverage = PASS/PLANNED. Label both explicitly and regenerate all summary percentages.

observation: The reconciled execution report describes CI-008 as P0, while the earlier supplied results ledger classifies CI-008 as P2. The revised summary also assigns a P0 not-run case to CI-008.
impact: Priority totals may be arithmetically consistent but no longer match the original approved spec without a documented version change.
required_action: Compare the exact hashed specification and index. Preserve the frozen priority or record an approved change with rationale/version bump; recalculate all priority totals from that source.

area: Evidence IDs do not match canonical test IDs
observation: The evidence manifest references legacy IDs such as R-001..R-010, K-001..K-014, H-001..H-016, G-001..G-018, Q-001..Q-010, N-001..N-008 and C-001..C-018, while the results CSV uses E2E-001, RPT-001, AI-001, EVID-001, CI-001, AUDIT-001 and RBAC-001 prefixes.
impact: Evidence may not join to test rows unambiguously.
required_action: Update the manifest to use canonical IDs exactly, or add an explicit, reviewed legacy-to-canonical mapping table. Validate every referenced ID exists in the current index.

area: Source files cited as execution evidence
observation: Several manifest entries hash source files such as test_auth.py and test_complaints.py and describe them as evidence of test passes. Source code proves what tests are defined, not that a particular run passed.
impact: Pass results are not reproducible from source-file hashes alone.
required_action: Attach actual pytest output/JUnit XML, Playwright JSON/HTML reports and traces, build logs, migration command output, and captured benchmark/header data. Use source hashes only as code provenance.

observation: The earlier evidence manifest records .github/workflows/ci.yml as 4,466 bytes, while the reconciled execution report says 2,285 bytes. Both claim the workflow was confirmed present.
impact: The files may come from different revisions or captures; the tested CI configuration is ambiguous.
required_action: Record the workflow blob SHA, file size, HEAD plus patch state, capture time, and actual workflow run ID/URL. Reconcile whether these represent the same version.

observation: The report verifies the workflow file exists and is configured, while CI-008 is NOT RUN because coverage flags are absent. No actual GitHub Actions run URL or run identifier is shown in the provided report.
impact: Presence/static inspection is not the same as an executed, successful CI run.
required_action: Describe workflow-file inspection separately from remote CI execution. Attach a real run URL/ID and job results; otherwise mark remote execution NOT VERIFIED.

area: Performance claims are too broad for evidence
observation: PERF-001 measures 100 sequential requests only to /api/v1/health, with p50 10.14 ms, p95 27.41 ms and a p99/max outlier of 785.8 ms. PERF-002..008 remain NOT RUN.
impact: A single sequential health endpoint benchmark cannot prove general app capacity or 250-user targets.
required_action: Label PERF-001 an exploratory health-endpoint baseline, include setup and raw timing data, define target thresholds before judging, and run the planned multi-user staged tests before claiming capacity readiness.

area: Crypto integrity language still overstates guarantees
observation: The reconciled architecture report continues to describe a SHA-256 report digest as 'immutable' and says the audit trail is immutable in places, despite the reconciliation saying terminology was corrected. A hash stored in the same mutable database is not itself an immutable signature or trusted timestamp.
impact: Could mislead reviewers about tamper resistance, non-repudiation, or evidentiary guarantees.
required_action: Use 'SHA-256 content-integrity digest checked against the stored reference' and 'access-controlled append-only application audit trail'. Do not claim immutability, non-repudiation, or digital signature unless a separate control proves it.

observation: Architecture claims four explicit personas (citizen, specialist, admin, system/superadmin), while workflows also define Police and AI/ML System Lead as distinct personas and report five-role E2E coverage.
impact: Permission scope and coverage become unclear; a role may be omitted from a matrix.
required_action: Publish one canonical role matrix showing every role, authority level, case scope, evidence visibility, report permissions, AI access, and admin actions. Clarify whether four tiers are privilege tiers or actual role count.

observation: The reports list hashes for a remediation patch, master spec, evidence files, and build output, but those underlying artifact files are not all included in the uploaded package here. A directory output such as frontend/dist/ also needs a defined hash method.
impact: This review can verify the claimed hashes are well-formed strings, not recompute them or confirm artifact contents.
required_action: Provide the patch, master spec, current test index/results CSV, evidence manifest, and raw artifacts. For directories, hash a deterministic archive or a manifest of relative file paths plus per-file hashes. Recompute hashes locally.

area: Role/session and suite assertions have broad mapping
observation: The evidence manifest associates small suites (for example 2–3 test functions) with many test-case requirements. That may be valid only if each test asserts all mapped expectations; the report does not include per-assertion coverage mapping in the pasted documents.
impact: The evidence ledger may imply stronger coverage than the actual assertions provide.
required_action: Add assertion-level mapping: canonical case ID -> test node ID -> assertion or scenario -> result artifact. If one test covers multiple criteria, document the exact assertion for each.

area: Operational gates differ between blocker and secondary gate documents
observation: The updated report lists secrets, ClamAV, and neural weights as primary blockers, while OP-001 through OP-004 add restore drills, coverage thresholds, TLS/reverse-proxy audits, and load benchmarks. Some executive sections only enumerate three blockers.
impact: The headline may understate requirements for a production approval even when detailed sections contain them.
required_action: Use one consolidated release-gate register and ensure the executive verdict names all mandatory gates, owners, validation evidence, and status.

area: Terminology '100% verified' conflicts with non-passing cases
observation: The report correctly says 209 PASS / 2 BLOCKED / 8 NOT RUN but also uses broad phrases such as 'fully validated' and '100% verified'.
impact: The audience may read it as all 219 cases executed and passed.
required_action: Restrict '100%' to the precise proven scope (e.g. 35/35 Playwright scenarios as reported). Describe the master suite as 209 passing, 2 blocked, 8 not run.
